headline: Meta plans a one-gigawatt, mostly gas-powered data center in Sturgeon County, Alberta, its first in Canada.
score_reason: Pool 7 lowered by 2: the announcement is from 8 Jul 2026, three months old; a 4 Oct republication adds nothing new.
importance_line: Alberta workers and towns get about 3,000 construction jobs and 300 permanent ones, Meta gets its largest data center outside the US, and the gas-fired power supply raises a climate and grid question that Meta's own figures do not answer.
summary: The Japan Times reports that Meta said on 8 Jul 2026 it will invest around US$10 billion (C$13 billion) in a data center in Sturgeon County, Alberta, its first in Canada and its largest outside the United States. The site, a large building of computers for AI work, would have one gigawatt of power capacity (the Times equates it to about 750,000 homes), run largely on natural gas that Meta says it is paying to generate and connect to Alberta's grid, and create 300 permanent jobs.
notes: Older news re-dated by EnergyNow on 4 Oct 2026; original article blocked, text read at The Japan Times. All figures are Meta's own.
